decisions.choice: if you return, return to me: Israel's turning must be a turning to the LORD himself
alternatives: if you return, Israel, you may come back (to your place, to favor)
decisions.reason: The verb "return" comes twice, and "to me" stands first in the second clause for emphasis. The call answers 3:10, where Judah turned back only "with falsehood": a real return is a return to the LORD himself. The second clause could also be read as a promise, "you may come back", restored to God's favor and the land (15:19 plays on the same verb in this way). Either way the condition is a return to God.

decisions.choice: detestable things: idols and the objects of foreign worship
decisions.reason: The word is used for idols and the gods they stand for, things the LORD finds loathsome (7:30; 13:27; 2 Kings 23:13, 24). Putting them away "from before me" means removing them from the LORD's presence, out of the land and the temple.

decisions.choice: wander: drift back and forth, stray
decisions.reason: The verb describes moving about with no settled place, as Cain was to be a wanderer (Genesis 4:12, 14). Here it pictures Israel drifting between the LORD and other gods (2:23, 36).

decisions.choice: the conditions run on into verse 2, where the result follows
decisions.reason: "If" governs several clauses (return, remove, do not wander, swear truly), and the promise for the nations comes only at the end of verse 2. The sentence continues across the verse division.

decisions.choice: detestable idols / disgusting idols ... wandering away from me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "idols" to show what the detestable things were (m2). Readable also says whom Israel wanders from, which the Hebrew leaves implied.

en.L: and swear, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," \q in truth, in justice and in righteousness, \q then nations will bless themselves by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} they will make their boast.
en.B: and swear, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," \q in truth, with justice and with righteousness, \q then the nations will bless themselves by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and take pride in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: and if you make your promises by saying, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," \q and you mean it, and do what is fair and right, \q then the nations will ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to bless them, and they will be proud to belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: "As the LORD lives": the oath that calls on the living God as witness
decisions.reason: Israel was to swear by the LORD's name and by no other god (Deuteronomy 6:13; 10:20; Jeremiah 12:16). The oath counts only when it is backed by truth, justice and righteousness; in 5:2 the people say "As the LORD lives" and swear falsely.

decisions.choice: nations will bless themselves in him: the promise to Abraham fulfilled through Israel's return
decisions.reason: The same form of the verb is used in the promise to Abraham that all nations will bless themselves by his offspring (Genesis 22:18; 26:4; compare 12:3). When Israel turns back to God with a true heart, the nations will see it and seek blessing from Israel's God. The reflexive form can mean that they will invoke his name when they bless, or that they will find blessing for themselves in him.

decisions.choice: in him: the LORD
decisions.reason: The nearest person named is the LORD, by whom Israel swears, and boasting "in the LORD" is a common phrase (9:23; Psalm 34:3). The pronoun could point to Israel, as the one through whom blessing comes in Genesis, but the oath and the boasting both look to God.

decisions.choice: you mean it, and do what is fair and right ... proud to belong to him
decisions.reason: Readable puts the three nouns "in truth, in justice and in righteousness" as what the person swearing does, and spells out "boast in him" as being proud to belong to him.

decisions.choice: [As] the LORD lives (Literal); As surely as the LORD lives (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew oath is literally "living is the LORD". Literal brackets the supplied "As"; Balanced and Readable use the oath wording of 12:16 and of 1 Samuel.

decisions.choice: "Vive el SEÑOR" (L); "Tan cierto como que el SEÑOR vive" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The oath formula as the Samuel terms note sets it for Spanish.

decisions.choice: Kama BWANA aishivyo
decisions.reason: The oath in the wording of the published 1 Kings 17:1 and 17:12; Literal brackets "Kama" as the English brackets "As".

source.text: כִּי־כֹ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֗ה לְאִ֤ישׁ יְהוּדָה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם נִ֥ירוּ לָכֶ֖ם נִ֑יר וְאַֽל־תִּזְרְע֖וּ אֶל־קוֹצִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: For thus says Yahweh to [the] man of Judah and to Jerusalem: Break up for yourselves fallow ground, and do not sow among thorns.

en.L: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the man of Judah and to Jerusalem: \q Break up for yourselves fallow ground, \q and do not sow among thorns.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this to the {{gender:people|men}} of Judah and to Jerusalem: \q Plow up your unplowed ground, \q and do not sow among thorns.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says to the people of Judah and Jerusalem: \q Your lives are like hard ground that needs plowing. Plow it up! \q Do not plant your seed among thorns.

es.L: Porque así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} al hombre de Judá y a Jerusalén: \q {{plural_you:Aren|Arad}} para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} el barbecho, \q y no {{plural_you:siembren|sembréis}} entre espinos.
es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto a la gente de Judá y a Jerusalén: \q {{plural_you:Aren|Arad}} la tierra que no ha sido arada, \q y no {{plural_you:siembren|sembréis}} entre espinos.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a la gente de Judá y de Jerusalén: \q {{plural_you:Sus vidas|Vuestras vidas}} son como tierra dura que necesita ser arada. ¡{{plural_you:Árenla|Aradla}}! \q No {{plural_you:siembren su semilla|sembréis vuestra semilla}} entre espinos.

sw.L: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi kwa mtu wa Yuda na kwa Yerusalemu: \q Jilimieni mashamba mapya, \q wala msipande kati ya miiba.
sw.B: Kwa maana hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awaambiavyo watu wa Yuda na Yerusalemu: \q Limeni mashamba yenu yasiyolimwa, \q wala msipande kati ya miiba.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analowaambia watu wa Yuda na Yerusalemu: \q Maisha yenu ni kama ardhi ngumu inayohitaji kulimwa. Ilimeni! \q Msipande mbegu zenu kati ya miiba.

decisions.choice: break up fallow ground: make a new start, as a farmer plows hard, neglected land before sowing
decisions.reason: Fallow ground has been left unplowed and has grown hard and weedy. Breaking it up is the first work before a new crop. Hosea uses the same words for seeking the LORD (Hosea 10:12): the people's lives must be turned over completely before anything good can grow.

decisions.choice: do not sow among thorns: do not add a show of repentance to lives still full of old sins
decisions.reason: Seed sown where thorns still grow is choked and comes to nothing (12:13; Genesis 3:18). A turning to God that leaves the old ways in place will not bear fruit.

decisions.choice: the man of Judah: everyone in Judah
decisions.reason: "Man" is singular here and stands for the whole population, men and women alike, as "inhabitant of Jerusalem" does (verse 4; Isaiah 5:3).

decisions.choice: the people of Judah
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the singular "man of Judah". Balanced and Readable say "people", since everyone in Judah is meant (m3).

decisions.choice: Your lives are like hard ground that needs plowing
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of plowing stands for, so that the reader does not take it as farming advice (m1).

decisions.choice: "la gente de Judá", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "gente" covers men and women, so the English gender setting needs no Spanish span; Literal keeps "el hombre de Judá".

decisions.choice: hivi ndivyo BWANA awaambiavyo
decisions.reason: The settled formula takes the verb "kuambia" here because the Hebrew names the people spoken to.

records.literal_gloss: Circumcise yourselves to Yahweh, and remove [the] foreskins of your heart, man of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, lest go out like fire my wrath and burn, and there is no one quenching, because of [the] evil of your deeds.

en.L: Be circumcised to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and remove the foreskins of your heart, \q man of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, \q or {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will go out like fire, and burn, and there will be no one to quench [it], \q because of the evil of your deeds.
en.B: Circumcise yourselves for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; circumcise your hearts, \q {{gender:people|men}} of Judah and people of Jerusalem, \q or {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will flare up like fire and burn, and no one will put it out, \q because of the evil you have done.
en.R: Circumcise yourselves to belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Circumcise your hearts: open them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q you people of Judah and Jerusalem. \q If you do not, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger will blaze out like a fire. It will burn, and no one will be able to put it out, \q because of the evil things you have done.

es.B: {{plural_you:Circuncídense|Circuncidaos}} para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}; {{plural_you:circunciden su corazón|circuncidad vuestro corazón}}, \q gente de Judá y habitantes de Jerusalén, \q o {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira estallará como fuego y arderá, y nadie la podrá apagar, \q por el mal que {{plural_you:han hecho|habéis hecho}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Circuncídense|Circuncidaos}} para pertenecer {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. {{plural_you:Circunciden su corazón|Circuncidad vuestro corazón}}: {{plural_you:ábranlo|abridlo}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, \q gente de Judá y de Jerusalén. \q Si no lo {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira se encenderá como un fuego. Arderá, y nadie la podrá apagar, \q por las cosas malas que {{plural_you:han hecho|habéis hecho}}.

sw.L: Jitahirini kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mkaondoe magovi ya mioyo yenu, \q enyi mtu wa Yuda na wakaaji wa Yerusalemu, \q ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} isije ikatoka kama moto, ikawaka, wala hakuna wa kuizima, \q kwa sababu ya uovu wa matendo yenu.
sw.B: Jitahirini kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; itahirini mioyo yenu, \q enyi watu wa Yuda na watu wa Yerusalemu, \q la sivyo ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itawaka kama moto, wala hakuna atakayeweza kuizima, \q kwa sababu ya maovu mliyoyatenda.
sw.R: Jitahirini ili muwe mali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Itahirini mioyo yenu, yaani, ifungueni kwangu, \q enyi watu wa Yuda na Yerusalemu. \q Msipofanya hivyo, hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itawaka kama moto. Itaunguza, wala hakuna mtu atakayeweza kuizima, \q kwa sababu ya mambo maovu mliyoyatenda.

decisions.choice: remove the foreskins of your heart: the command of Deuteronomy 10:16
decisions.reason: Moses told Israel to "circumcise the foreskin of your heart" (Deuteronomy 10:16) and promised that the LORD would one day do it himself (Deuteronomy 30:6). Jeremiah repeats the command to a people who bear the sign in their bodies but not in their hearts (9:24-25).

decisions.choice: circumcise yourselves to the LORD: make the covenant sign true on the inside, belonging wholly to him
decisions.reason: Circumcision was the sign of the covenant on the body (Genesis 17:10-14). An uncircumcised heart is closed and unwilling to hear (Leviticus 26:41; Jeremiah 6:10 uses the same picture for the ear). To circumcise oneself "to the LORD" is to remove what closes the heart to him and to give oneself to him.

decisions.choice: my wrath will go out like fire, with no one to quench it: a judgment that cannot be stopped once it starts
decisions.reason: The same words return in 21:12 and Amos 5:6. A fire that no one can put out is a judgment that runs its course; the call to repent comes before it starts.

decisions.choice: circumcise your hearts
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the wording of Deuteronomy 10:16, which leaves out "foreskins" because "circumcise your hearts" already carries the picture. Literal keeps the full wording. Readable adds what it means, "open them to me", as Deuteronomy 10:16 does.

decisions.choice: people of Judah and (people of) Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, the singular "man" and the word "inhabitants" mean everyone who lives there.

decisions.choice: "quiten los prepucios de su corazón" (L); "circunciden su corazón" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of Deuteronomy 10:16; Balanced and Readable use the shorter phrase, as the English levels do.

decisions.choice: magovi ya mioyo yenu (Literal); itahirini mioyo yenu (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The words of Deuteronomy 10:16 (meaning decision m1): "govi", foreskin, and "kutahiri", to circumcise, as the Pentateuch has them; the same wording returns at 9:25.

records.literal_gloss: Declare in Judah, and in Jerusalem proclaim, and say: Blow [the] shofar in the land; call out, fill, and say: Gather yourselves and let us go into [the] cities of the fortification.

en.L: Declare in Judah, and in Jerusalem proclaim, and say, \q "Blow the trumpet in the land!" \q Cry out, [with] full [voice], and say, \q "Gather together, and let us go into the fortified cities!"
en.B: Announce it in Judah, proclaim it in Jerusalem, and say, \q "Blow the ram's horn throughout the land!" \q Shout at the top of your voice and say, \q "Gather together! Let us go into the fortified cities!"
en.R: Announce this in Judah and in Jerusalem. Tell them: \q "Blow the trumpet everywhere in the land!" \q Shout as loud as you can: \q "Come together! Let us run to the cities with strong walls!"

es.L: {{plural_you:Anuncien|Anunciad}} en Judá, y en Jerusalén {{plural_you:proclamen|proclamad}}, y {{plural_you:digan|decid}}: \q «¡{{plural_you:Toquen|Tocad}} la trompeta en la tierra!». \q {{plural_you:Griten|Gritad}} a plena [voz] y {{plural_you:digan|decid}}: \q «¡{{plural_you:Reúnanse|Reuníos}}, y entremos en las ciudades fortificadas!».
es.B: {{plural_you:Anúncienlo|Anunciadlo}} en Judá, {{plural_you:proclámenlo|proclamadlo}} en Jerusalén, y {{plural_you:digan|decid}}: \q «¡{{plural_you:Toquen|Tocad}} el cuerno de carnero por todo el país!». \q {{plural_you:Griten|Gritad}} a voz en cuello y {{plural_you:digan|decid}}: \q «¡{{plural_you:Reúnanse|Reuníos}}! ¡Entremos en las ciudades fortificadas!».
es.R: {{plural_you:Anuncien|Anunciad}} esto en Judá y en Jerusalén. {{plural_you:Díganles|Decidles}}: \q «¡{{plural_you:Toquen|Tocad}} la trompeta por todo el país!». \q {{plural_you:Griten|Gritad}} con todas {{plural_you:sus fuerzas|vuestras fuerzas}}: \q «¡{{plural_you:Júntense|Juntaos}}! ¡Corramos a las ciudades con murallas fuertes!».

sw.L: Tangazeni katika Yuda, na katika Yerusalemu hubirini, mkaseme, \q "Pigeni baragumu katika nchi!" \q Pazeni sauti [kwa] nguvu, mkaseme, \q "Kusanyikeni, na tuingie katika miji yenye ngome!"
sw.B: Tangazeni katika Yuda, hubirini katika Yerusalemu, mseme, \q "Pigeni baragumu katika nchi yote!" \q Pigeni kelele kwa sauti kuu mkiseme, \q "Kusanyikeni! Tuingie katika miji yenye ngome!"
sw.R: Tangazeni jambo hili katika Yuda na katika Yerusalemu. Waambieni: \q "Pigeni baragumu kila mahali katika nchi!" \q Pigeni kelele kwa sauti yenu yote: \q "Kusanyikeni! Tukimbilie miji yenye kuta imara!"

decisions.choice: the shofar blown in the land: the alarm for an enemy attack
decisions.reason: The shofar, a ram's horn, was blown to warn of an enemy and to call people to arms or to shelter (6:1; Hosea 5:8; Amos 3:6). Here it warns of the invader of verses 6-7.

decisions.choice: call out, fill: cry with a full voice
decisions.reason: The two verbs stand side by side with no object. "Fill" means fill the voice: shout loudly. The heralds are to cry the warning as loud as they can (12:6 has "they call after you fully").

decisions.choice: fortified cities: walled towns where people from the open country took refuge
decisions.reason: When an army invaded, people left their villages and fields for the walled towns (8:14; 35:11). The cry shows that the danger is close.

decisions.choice: the LORD sends heralds through the land; what they are to cry is quoted
decisions.reason: The commands are plural: heralds are told to spread the alarm. The words of the alarm itself, "Blow ..." and "Gather ...", are what they are to say.

decisions.choice: trumpet (L, R); ram's horn (B)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for the shofar, as in Isaiah: Literal and Readable say "trumpet", Balanced "ram's horn" (m1).

decisions.choice: cities with strong walls
decisions.reason: Readable says what made a city "fortified" (m3).

decisions.choice: "trompeta" (L, R); "cuerno de carnero" (B)
decisions.reason: As the English levels: Balanced names the ram's horn, Literal and Readable use the familiar word. The cries quoted for the heralds are plural commands and take the plural you setting too.

decisions.choice: baragumu
decisions.reason: The shofar is "baragumu", the horn trumpet, at every level, as the published 1 Chronicles 15:28 distinguishes it from the metal "tarumbeta"; the English levels vary between "trumpet" and "ram's horn".

source.text: שְׂאוּ־נֵ֣ס צִיּ֔וֹנָה הָעִ֖יזוּ אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹ֑דוּ כִּ֣י רָעָ֗ה אָנֹכִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא מִצָּפ֖וֹן וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּדֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: Lift up a signal flag toward Zion; flee for safety, do not stand still, for evil I am bringing from [the] north, and great destruction.

en.L: Lift up a signal flag toward Zion; \q flee for safety, do not stand still! \q For evil I am bringing from the north, and a great breaking.
en.B: Raise a signal flag toward Zion! \q Run for safety; do not wait! \q For I am bringing disaster from the north, a great and crushing ruin.
en.R: Put up a signal flag that points the way to Zion! \q Run for safety! Do not wait! \q For I am bringing disaster from the north. It will crush everything.

es.L: {{plural_you:Alcen|Alzad}} bandera hacia Sion; \q ¡{{plural_you:huyan para salvarse, no se detengan|huid para salvaros, no os detengáis}}! \q Porque yo traigo del norte el mal, y un gran quebranto.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Alcen|Alzad}} una bandera hacia Sion! \q ¡{{plural_you:Corran a ponerse|Corred a poneros}} a salvo; no {{plural_you:esperen|esperéis}}! \q Porque yo traigo del norte la desgracia, una ruina grande y aplastante.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Pongan|Poned}} una bandera que señale el camino a Sion! \q ¡{{plural_you:Corran a ponerse|Corred a poneros}} a salvo! ¡No {{plural_you:esperen|esperéis}}! \q Porque yo traigo la desgracia desde el norte. Lo aplastará todo.

sw.L: Inueni bendera kuelekea Sayuni; \q kimbieni mpate salama, msisimame! \q Kwa maana ninaleta mabaya kutoka kaskazini, na uvunjifu mkuu.
sw.B: Inueni bendera kuelekea Sayuni! \q Kimbieni mpate usalama; msingoje! \q Kwa maana ninaleta maafa kutoka kaskazini, maangamizi makuu yanayoponda.
sw.R: Wekeni bendera inayoonyesha njia ya kwenda Sayuni! \q Kimbieni mpate usalama! Msingoje! \q Kwa maana ninaleta maafa kutoka kaskazini. Yataponda kila kitu.

decisions.choice: a signal flag toward Zion: a banner on a pole showing refugees the way to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: A signal flag was raised on a pole or a hilltop to call people together or show them where to go (Isaiah 5:26; 11:12). Here it points the people of the countryside to Zion, Jerusalem, as the place of refuge.

decisions.choice: evil: disaster, harm
decisions.reason: The word means what is bad, whether wrongdoing or the harm that comes on people. Here it is the disaster the LORD brings as judgment, not wrongdoing on his part (as in Isaiah 45:7; Jeremiah 1:14).

decisions.choice: from the north: the invader foretold in Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: In 1:13-15 disaster boils over "from the north". The enemy is not named in these chapters (6:1, 22); later it is named as Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar (20:4; 25:9). Armies from Mesopotamia came into Israel from the north, along the curve of fertile land.

decisions.choice: great destruction: a great breaking, a crash
decisions.reason: The word means breaking or fracture, as of a bone or a wall. It returns in verse 20 and through the book for the collapse of the nation (6:1; 8:21; 14:17).

decisions.choice: a great and crushing ruin / It will crush everything
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the picture of breaking in "destruction" (m4).

decisions.choice: "bandera"
decisions.reason: The signal flag (nes) is "bandera" at every level, as the terms note sets it.

source.text: עָלָ֤ה אַרְיֵה֙ מִֽסֻּבְּכ֔וֹ וּמַשְׁחִ֣ית גּוֹיִ֔ם נָסַ֖ע יָצָ֣א מִמְּקֹמ֑וֹ לָשׂ֤וּם אַרְצֵךְ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה עָרַ֥יִךְ תִּצֶּ֖ינָה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: Has gone up a lion from his thicket, and a destroyer of nations has set out; he has gone out from his place to make your land a waste; your cities will be laid in ruins, without inhabitant.

en.L: A lion has come up from his thicket, \q and a destroyer of nations has set out; \q he has gone out from his place \q to make your land a waste; \q your cities will fall in ruins, without inhabitant.
en.B: A lion has left his thicket; \q a destroyer of nations has broken camp. \q He has left his place \q to make your land a wasteland. \q Your towns will lie in ruins, with no one living in them.
en.R: A lion has come out of the bushes where it hides. \q One who destroys nations is on the march. \q He has left his home \q to turn your land into a wasteland. \q Your towns will be ruins, and no one will live in them.

es.L: Ha subido el león de su espesura, \q y el destructor de naciones se ha puesto en marcha; \q ha salido de su lugar \q para convertir tu tierra en desolación; \q tus ciudades quedarán en ruinas, sin habitante.
es.B: Un león ha dejado su espesura; \q un destructor de naciones ha levantado el campamento. \q Ha salido de su lugar \q para convertir tu tierra en un desierto. \q Tus ciudades quedarán en ruinas, sin nadie que viva en ellas.
es.R: Un león ha salido de los matorrales donde se esconde. \q Uno que destruye naciones está en marcha. \q Ha salido de su casa \q para convertir tu tierra en un desierto. \q Tus ciudades serán ruinas, y nadie vivirá en ellas.

sw.L: Simba amepanda kutoka kichakani mwake, \q naye mwangamizaji wa mataifa ameondoka; \q ametoka mahali pake \q aifanye nchi yako kuwa ukiwa; \q miji yako itaanguka kuwa magofu, bila mkaaji.
sw.B: Simba ametoka kichakani mwake; \q mwangamizaji wa mataifa ameng'oa kambi yake. \q Ameondoka mahali pake \q ili aifanye nchi yako kuwa jangwa. \q Miji yako itakuwa magofu, bila mtu wa kuishi ndani yake.
sw.R: Simba ametoka vichakani anakojificha. \q Yeye anayeangamiza mataifa yuko safarini. \q Ameondoka nyumbani kwake \q ili aigeuze nchi yako kuwa jangwa. \q Miji yako itakuwa magofu, wala hakuna mtu atakayeishi humo.

decisions.choice: a lion ... a destroyer of nations: the invading king and his army
decisions.reason: The lion is a picture of the enemy from the north (verse 6), who leaves his lair to hunt (2:15; 5:6; 50:17, where the lion is named as the king of Babylon). "Destroyer of nations" says plainly what the lion is.

decisions.choice: set out: pulled up the tent pegs, broke camp
decisions.reason: The verb is used for breaking camp and moving on (Genesis 35:5; Numbers 10:12). The army is already on the move.

decisions.choice: a waste ... laid in ruins: the land made desolate, the towns emptied
decisions.reason: The first word means a place so ruined that people are appalled at it (2:15; 5:30). The second verb means to be laid waste, to fall in ruins; with "without inhabitant" it pictures towns left empty.

decisions.choice: the bushes where it hides
decisions.reason: Readable explains "thicket", the dense undergrowth where a lion lies hidden.

source.text: עַל־זֹ֛את חִגְר֥וּ שַׂקִּ֖ים סִפְד֣וּ וְהֵילִ֑ילוּ כִּ֥י לֹא־שָׁ֛ב חֲר֥וֹן אַף־יְהֹוָ֖ה מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Because of this put on sackcloth, lament and wail, for not has turned back [the] burning of [the] anger of Yahweh from us.

en.L: Because of this, gird on sackcloth, lament and wail; \q for the burning anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has not turned back from us.
en.B: So dress in sackcloth, lament and wail, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s fierce anger has still not turned away from us.
en.R: So put on rough clothes to show your sorrow. Mourn and cry out in grief! \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is still burning with anger against us. It has not turned away from us.

es.L: Por esto, {{plural_you:cíñanse|ceñíos}} de cilicio, {{plural_you:lamenten y giman|lamentad y gemid}}; \q porque el ardor de la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} no se ha apartado de nosotros.
es.B: Por eso, {{plural_you:vístanse|vestíos}} de cilicio, {{plural_you:lamenten y giman|lamentad y gemid}}, \q porque la ardiente ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} todavía no se ha apartado de nosotros.
es.R: Por eso, {{plural_you:vístanse|vestíos}} con ropa áspera de luto. ¡{{plural_you:Lloren y giman|Llorad y gemid}} de tristeza! \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} sigue ardiendo de ira contra nosotros. Su enojo no se ha apartado de nosotros.

sw.L: Kwa sababu ya hili jifungeni nguo za magunia, ombolezeni na kupiga yowe; \q kwa maana hasira kali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} haijarudi nyuma kutoka kwetu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo vaeni nguo za magunia, ombolezeni na kulia kwa sauti, \q kwa maana hasira kali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} bado haijatuacha.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo vaeni nguo za magunia kuonyesha huzuni yenu. Ombolezeni na kulia kwa uchungu! \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} bado anawaka hasira juu yetu. Hasira yake haijatuacha.

decisions.choice: put on sackcloth: dress in mourning
decisions.reason: Sackcloth was rough cloth of goat hair, tied around the waist in times of grief, repentance or disaster (6:26; Genesis 37:34; Isaiah 22:12).

decisions.choice: the burning of the anger of the LORD: his fierce anger
decisions.reason: The word for anger also means "nose", from the flaring nostrils of an angry person; with "burning" it describes anger at its height (verse 26; 25:37; Exodus 32:12).

decisions.choice: us: the prophet speaks as one of the people
decisions.reason: The prophet calls the people to mourn and counts himself among those under God's anger, as he does again in verse 13.

decisions.choice: rough clothes to show your sorrow ... cry out in grief
decisions.reason: Readable explains what sackcloth was for (m1) and uses the book-wide Readable wording "cry out in grief" for "wail", as Isaiah does.

decisions.choice: "cilicio" (L, B); "ropa áspera de luto" (R)
decisions.reason: Sackcloth is "cilicio" as the Samuel terms note sets it; Readable says what it was and why it was worn, as the English does.

source.text: וְהָיָ֤ה בַיּוֹם־הַהוּא֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה יֹאבַ֥ד לֵב־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְלֵ֣ב הַשָּׂרִ֑ים וְנָשַׁ֨מּוּ֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים וְהַנְּבִיאִ֖ים יִתְמָֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be in the day that, declares Yahweh, will perish [the] heart of the king and [the] heart of the officials, and will be appalled the priests, and the prophets will be astounded.

en.L: And it will be in that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q [that] the heart of the king will fail, and the heart of the princes; \q and the priests will be appalled, \q and the prophets will be astounded.
en.B: On that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the king and the officials will lose heart; \q the priests will be horrified, \q and the prophets will be stunned.
en.R: At that time, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the king and his leaders will lose their courage. \q The priests will be shocked, \q and the prophets will be stunned.

es.L: Y sucederá en aquel día, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q [que] desfallecerá el corazón del rey y el corazón de los príncipes; \q y los sacerdotes quedarán espantados, \q y los profetas, atónitos.
es.B: Aquel día, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q el rey y los jefes perderán el valor; \q los sacerdotes se horrorizarán, \q y los profetas quedarán pasmados.
es.R: En ese tiempo, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q el rey y sus líderes perderán el valor. \q Los sacerdotes quedarán impactados, \q y los profetas, pasmados.

sw.L: Na itakuwa katika siku ile, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q moyo wa mfalme utazimia, na moyo wa wakuu; \q na makuhani watashangaa, \q na manabii watastaajabu.
sw.B: Siku hiyo, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q mfalme na maafisa watakata tamaa; \q makuhani watatishika, \q na manabii watapigwa na bumbuazi.
sw.R: Wakati huo, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q mfalme na viongozi wake watakosa ujasiri. \q Makuhani watashtuka, \q na manabii watapigwa na bumbuazi.

decisions.choice: the heart will perish: courage will fail
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and courage. When it "perishes" a person loses nerve and cannot think what to do (Psalm 76:6 speaks of the stout-hearted stripped of strength).

decisions.choice: king, officials, priests, prophets: all who were meant to lead the nation
decisions.reason: Jeremiah names the same four groups as those who have led Judah astray (2:26; 8:1; 32:32). The prophets who promised peace (verse 10; 6:14) will be the most dumbfounded.

decisions.choice: princes (L), officials (B), leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for the king's chief men.

decisions.choice: "en aquel día" (L); "aquel día" (B); "en ese tiempo" (R)
decisions.reason: "In that day" as the terms note sets it for Spanish at each level.

decisions.choice: katika siku ile (Literal); siku hiyo (Balanced); wakati huo (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording of "in that day", as the terms note sets it.

source.text: וָאֹמַ֞ר אֲהָ֣הּ׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אָכֵן֩ הַשֵּׁ֨א הִשֵּׁ֜אתָ לָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וְלִירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם לֵאמֹ֔ר שָׁל֖וֹם יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם וְנָגְעָ֥ה חֶ֖רֶב עַד־הַנָּֽפֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said, Alas, Lord Yahweh, surely deceiving you have deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, Peace will be to you; and has reached [the] sword to the throat.

en.L: Then I said, "Alas, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! Surely {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have greatly deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, \q 'You will have peace,' \q while the sword has reached to the throat!"
en.B: Then I said, "Oh, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, truly {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have led this people and Jerusalem far astray with the words, \q 'You will have peace,' \q while the sword is pressing at their throats!"
en.R: Then I said, "Oh, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! You have truly fooled these people and Jerusalem! They were told, \q 'You will have peace.' \q But now a sword is at their throats!"

es.L: Entonces dije: «¡Ah, Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}! Ciertamente {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has engañado del todo a este pueblo y a Jerusalén, diciendo: \q “Tendrán paz”, \q mientras la espada ha llegado hasta la garganta».
es.B: Entonces dije: «¡Ay, Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, de verdad {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has engañado por completo a este pueblo y a Jerusalén con las palabras: \q “Tendrán paz”, \q mientras la espada les aprieta la garganta!».
es.R: Entonces dije: «¡Oh no, Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}! ¡De verdad has engañado a esta gente y a Jerusalén! Se les dijo: \q “Tendrán paz”. \q ¡Pero ahora tienen una espada en la garganta!».

sw.L: Ndipo nikasema, "Ole wangu, Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}! Hakika {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umewadanganya sana watu hawa na Yerusalemu, ukisema, \q 'Mtakuwa na amani,' \q hali upanga umefika mpaka kooni!"
sw.B: Ndipo nikasema, "Ee Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}, kweli umewapotosha sana watu hawa na Yerusalemu kwa maneno, \q 'Mtakuwa na amani,' \q hali upanga unawabana kooni!"
sw.R: Ndipo nikasema, "Hapana, Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}! Kweli umewadanganya watu hawa na Yerusalemu! Waliambiwa, \q 'Mtakuwa na amani.' \q Lakini sasa upanga uko shingoni mwao!"

decisions.choice: you have deceived this people: the prophet's grieving complaint that God let the false promise of peace stand
alternatives: God himself sent the message of peace
the people deceived themselves, and the prophet speaks loosely
decisions.reason: The verb means to lead astray with false hope (2 Kings 18:29; 19:10; Jeremiah 29:8). The prophets of Jeremiah's day kept promising "peace" (6:14; 14:13; 23:17), and Jeremiah, in anguish, speaks as if God were responsible, because God allowed their message to go unchecked. Elsewhere the LORD says plainly that he did not send them (14:14; 23:21). Scripture can speak of God giving those who refuse the truth over to a lying message (1 Kings 22:20-23; Ezekiel 14:9). The words are a cry of grief like the laments of 15:18 and 20:7, not a teaching that God lies (Numbers 23:19).

decisions.choice: and I said: the prophet speaks
alternatives: and they will say: the leaders of verse 9 speak these words
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "and I said", so the words are Jeremiah's. Some Greek manuscripts are reported to read "and they will say" or "and they said", which would make the complaint that of the stunned priests and prophets of verse 9. The Hebrew reading is kept.

decisions.choice: surely deceiving you have deceived: the verb doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated, which strengthens it: "you have utterly deceived". The opening word "surely" adds to the force of the complaint.

decisions.choice: the sword has reached to the throat: their very life is under threat
decisions.reason: The word for "throat" also means life or self. The people were promised peace while the enemy's sword was already at their necks.

decisions.choice: Alas (L); Oh (B, R) ... Lord GOD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has a cry of dismay followed by "my Lord" and the divine name, written "Lord GOD" (or "Lord Yahweh" by the reader's setting) so that "Lord" is not written twice, as in Joshua 7:7.

decisions.choice: They were told
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "saying" does not say who spoke the words of peace. Readable keeps that open with "They were told" rather than naming God or the prophets as the speaker.

source.text: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא יֵאָמֵ֤ר לָֽעָם־הַזֶּה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם ר֣וּחַ צַ֤ח שְׁפָיִים֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר דֶּ֖רֶךְ בַּת־עַמִּ֑י ל֥וֹא לִזְר֖וֹת וְל֥וֹא לְהָבַֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: At the time that it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem: A wind hot of [the] bare heights in the wilderness [is the] way of [the] daughter of my people, not to winnow and not to cleanse;

en.L: At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem: \q "A scorching wind from the bare heights in the wilderness \q [comes] toward the daughter of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q not to winnow and not to cleanse;
en.B: At that time this people and Jerusalem will be told: \q "A scorching wind off the bare hills in the desert \q is blowing toward {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dear people, \q not to winnow and not to clean the grain;
en.R: At that time these people and Jerusalem will be told: \q "A burning hot wind is blowing from the bare hills in the desert \q toward {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q It is not the gentle wind that farmers use to separate the grain from the straw.

es.L: En aquel tiempo se dirá a este pueblo y a Jerusalén: \q «Un viento abrasador de las alturas desnudas del desierto \q [viene] hacia la hija de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, \q no para aventar ni para limpiar;
es.B: En aquel tiempo se le dirá a este pueblo y a Jerusalén: \q «Un viento abrasador de las colinas peladas del desierto \q sopla hacia {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} querido pueblo, \q no para aventar ni para limpiar el grano;
es.R: En ese tiempo se le dirá a esta gente y a Jerusalén: \q «Un viento caliente y abrasador sopla desde las colinas peladas del desierto \q hacia {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo. \q No es la brisa suave que usan los campesinos para separar el grano de la paja.

sw.L: Wakati ule itasemwa kwa watu hawa na kwa Yerusalemu: \q "Upepo wa moto kutoka vilele vilivyo wazi nyikani \q [unakuja] kuelekea binti wa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, \q si kupepeta wala si kusafisha;
sw.B: Wakati huo watu hawa na Yerusalemu wataambiwa: \q "Upepo wa moto kutoka vilima vilivyo wazi jangwani \q unavuma kuelekea watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wapendwa, \q si wa kupepeta wala wa kusafisha nafaka;
sw.R: Wakati huo watu hawa na Yerusalemu wataambiwa: \q "Upepo wenye joto kali unavuma kutoka vilima vilivyo wazi jangwani \q kuelekea watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. \q Si upepo mwanana ambao wakulima huutumia kutenganisha nafaka na makapi.

decisions.choice: a scorching wind from the bare heights in the wilderness: the hot east wind off the desert
decisions.reason: A dry, burning wind blows in from the eastern desert, withering plants and bringing dust (18:17; Hosea 13:15). The coming army will sweep over the land like it.

decisions.choice: not to winnow and not to cleanse: not the light breeze used to separate grain from chaff
decisions.reason: Farmers tossed threshed grain into the air on a breezy day; the wind carried off the chaff and the grain fell back clean (15:7; Ruth 3:2). This wind is far too strong for that (verse 12): it does not sift the people, it sweeps everything away.

decisions.choice: the daughter of my people: God's people spoken of with tenderness, as a daughter
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures the people as a beloved daughter, especially when they suffer (8:11, 19-23; 14:17; Lamentations 2:11). It is a term of affection and grief, not a separate group within the people.

decisions.choice: what will be said runs on to the end of verse 12, where the LORD speaks of himself
decisions.reason: The words of the announcement continue into verse 12, which speaks of the wind coming "for me" and ends with "I will speak judgments". The message announced to the people is the LORD's own.

decisions.choice: the daughter of my people (L); my dear people (B); my people (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for this phrase, decided here at its first use in Jeremiah. Literal keeps the Hebrew picture; Balanced keeps its tenderness in "my dear people"; Readable says simply "my people" (m3).

decisions.choice: to clean the grain / the gentle wind that farmers use to separate the grain from the straw
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what winnowing and cleansing are done to, and Readable explains the practice (m2).

decisions.choice: "la hija de mi pueblo" (L); "mi querido pueblo" (B); "mi pueblo" (R)
decisions.reason: Bat-'ammi, the people spoken of tenderly as a daughter, at each level as the English Jeremiah note sets it; the same wording returns through the book.

decisions.choice: binti wa watu wangu (Literal); watu wangu wapendwa (Balanced); watu wangu (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording of bat-'ammi, as the terms note sets it; it returns often in chapters 6-9 and 14.

source.text: ר֧וּחַ מָלֵ֛א מֵאֵ֖לֶּה יָ֣בוֹא לִ֑י עַתָּ֕ה גַּם־אֲנִ֛י אֲדַבֵּ֥ר מִשְׁפָּטִ֖ים אוֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: a wind full from these comes for me; now also I will speak judgments [with] them.

en.L: a wind too strong for these comes for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q Now I also will speak judgments against them."
en.B: a wind too strong for that comes at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} command. \q Now I, too, will pronounce judgment on them."
en.R: The wind I send is much too strong for that. \q Now I will announce {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sentence against them."

es.L: un viento demasiado fuerte para eso viene por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. \q Ahora también yo pronunciaré juicios contra ellos».
es.B: un viento demasiado fuerte para eso viene por orden {{deity_pronoun:mía|Mía}}. \q Ahora yo también pronunciaré sentencia contra ellos».
es.R: El viento que yo envío es demasiado fuerte para eso. \q Ahora anunciaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sentencia contra ellos».

sw.L: upepo ulio na nguvu kupita hayo unakuja kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Sasa mimi nami nitatamka hukumu juu yao."
sw.B: upepo wenye nguvu kupita hayo unakuja kwa amri {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Sasa mimi pia nitatamka hukumu juu yao."
sw.R: Upepo ninaoutuma una nguvu kupita kiasi kwa kazi hiyo. \q Sasa nitatangaza hukumu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} juu yao."

decisions.choice: too full for these: too strong for winnowing and cleansing
decisions.reason: "Full" here means strong, at full force. "These" points back to the winnowing and cleansing of verse 11: the wind is too violent for such work.

decisions.choice: for me: at my bidding, in my service
decisions.reason: The wind comes "for me", that is, on the LORD's errand. The enemy army is his instrument of judgment, as Babylon is called his servant in 25:9.

decisions.choice: speak judgments with them: pass sentence on them, as a judge does in court
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in 1:16 for the LORD's sentence on his people, and in 39:5 for the king of Babylon passing sentence on Zedekiah. "I also" sets the LORD's verdict against what the people have done.

decisions.choice: at my command / The wind I send
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what "for me" means (m2).

source.text: הִנֵּ֣ה׀כַּעֲנָנִ֣ים יַעֲלֶ֗ה וְכַסּוּפָה֙ מַרְכְּבוֹתָ֔יו קַלּ֥וּ מִנְּשָׁרִ֖ים סוּסָ֑יו א֥וֹי לָ֖נוּ כִּ֥י שֻׁדָּֽדְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, like clouds he comes up, and like the storm wind his chariots; swifter than eagles his horses. Woe to us, for we are devastated!

en.L: Look, like clouds he comes up, and like the storm wind [are] his chariots; \q his horses are swifter than eagles. \q "Woe to us, for we are devastated!"
en.B: See, he rises like gathering clouds, his chariots like a storm wind; \q his horses are quicker than eagles. \q "Woe to us! We are ruined!"
en.R: Look! The enemy is coming like storm clouds. His chariots race like a whirlwind. \q His horses are faster than eagles. \q "How terrible this is for us! We are ruined!"

es.L: He aquí, como nubes sube, y como torbellino [son] sus carros; \q sus caballos son más veloces que las águilas. \q «¡Ay de nosotros, porque estamos arruinados!».
es.B: ¡Mira! Se levanta como nubes que se juntan, sus carros como un torbellino; \q sus caballos son más rápidos que las águilas. \q «¡Ay de nosotros! ¡Estamos perdidos!».
es.R: ¡Mira! El enemigo viene como nubes de tormenta. Sus carros corren como un torbellino. \q Sus caballos son más veloces que las águilas. \q «¡Qué terrible es esto para nosotros! ¡Estamos perdidos!».

sw.L: Tazama, anapanda kama mawingu, na magari yake [ni] kama kimbunga; \q farasi wake ni wepesi kuliko tai. \q "Ole wetu, kwa maana tumeangamizwa!"
sw.B: Tazama, anainuka kama mawingu yanayokusanyika, magari yake kama kimbunga; \q farasi wake ni wepesi kuliko tai. \q "Ole wetu! Tumeangamia!"
sw.R: Tazama! Adui anakuja kama mawingu ya dhoruba. Magari yake ya vita yanakwenda kasi kama kimbunga. \q Farasi wake ni wepesi kuliko tai. \q "Itakuwa vibaya sana kwetu! Tumeangamia!"

decisions.choice: he: the invader, the lion and destroyer of verse 7
decisions.reason: No subject is named. The verb is singular and the chariots and horses are "his", so the one coming is the enemy king with his army (verse 7).

decisions.choice: eagles: large birds of prey, eagles or vultures
decisions.reason: The word covers the great birds of prey. It is used for the speed of an attacking nation in Deuteronomy 28:49 and Habakkuk 1:8.

decisions.choice: woe to us: the people's cry breaks in
decisions.reason: The voice changes: the people, seeing the army coming, cry out. Their words are set apart as a quotation.

decisions.choice: The enemy ... How terrible this is for us
decisions.reason: Readable names "the enemy" as the one who comes (m1), and uses the book-wide Readable wording for a cry of "woe" said of oneself.

decisions.choice: "¡Ay de nosotros!" (L, B); "¡Qué terrible es esto para nosotros!" (R)
decisions.reason: Woe said of oneself, as the terms note sets it for Spanish.

decisions.choice: Ole wetu (Literal, Balanced); Itakuwa vibaya sana kwetu (Readable)
decisions.reason: Hoy and 'oy are worded as the terms note sets them, Readable as Luke 6:24.

source.text: כַּבְּסִ֨י מֵרָעָ֤ה לִבֵּךְ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לְמַ֖עַן תִּוָּשֵׁ֑עִי עַד־מָתַ֛י תָּלִ֥ין בְּקִרְבֵּ֖ךְ מַחְשְׁב֥וֹת אוֹנֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Wash from evil your heart, Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. Until when will lodge within you thoughts of your wickedness?

en.L: Wash your heart from evil, Jerusalem, \q so that you may be saved. \q How long will the thoughts of your wickedness lodge within you?
en.B: Jerusalem, wash the evil from your heart, \q so that you may be saved. \q How long will you let your wicked schemes make their home in you?
en.R: Jerusalem, wash the evil out of your heart, \q so that you can be saved. \q How long will you keep thinking evil thoughts?

es.L: Lava tu corazón de la maldad, Jerusalén, \q para que seas salva. \q ¿Hasta cuándo alojarás dentro de ti tus pensamientos de iniquidad?
es.B: Jerusalén, lava la maldad de tu corazón, \q para que seas salvada. \q ¿Hasta cuándo dejarás que tus planes perversos vivan dentro de ti?
es.R: Jerusalén, lava la maldad de tu corazón \q para que puedas ser salvada. \q ¿Hasta cuándo seguirás teniendo pensamientos malos?

sw.L: Uoshe moyo wako uache uovu, Yerusalemu, \q upate kuokolewa. \q Mawazo yako ya uovu yatakaa ndani yako hata lini?
sw.B: Yerusalemu, safisha moyo wako uondoe uovu, \q upate kuokolewa. \q Utaruhusu mipango yako miovu ifanye makao ndani yako hadi lini?
sw.R: Yerusalemu, osha uovu uondoke moyoni mwako, \q ili uweze kuokolewa. \q Utaendelea kuwaza mawazo maovu hadi lini?

decisions.choice: wash your heart from evil: be cleansed within
decisions.reason: The verb is used for washing clothes. Here it is the inner person that must be scrubbed clean (2:22; Isaiah 1:16; Psalm 51:4, 9). Even now, with the enemy coming, there is still a way to be saved.

decisions.choice: lodge: stay the night, settle in as a guest
decisions.reason: The verb means to spend the night. Wicked thoughts are pictured as guests who have moved in and will not leave.

decisions.choice: thoughts of your wickedness: plans for doing wrong
decisions.reason: The first word means plans or schemes; the second means trouble or wickedness, harm done to others. The same word means "disaster" in verse 15: the evil they plan brings evil on them.

decisions.choice: make their home in you
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of guests settling in (m2) in a natural phrase.

source.text: כִּ֛י ק֥וֹל מַגִּ֖יד מִדָּ֑ן וּמַשְׁמִ֥יעַ אָ֖וֶן מֵהַ֥ר אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: For a voice declaring from Dan, and proclaiming trouble from [the] hill country of Ephraim.

en.L: For a voice is declaring from Dan, \q and proclaiming trouble from the hill country of Ephraim.
en.B: For a voice is announcing from Dan, \q proclaiming disaster from the hill country of Ephraim.
en.R: Listen! A messenger is bringing news from Dan in the far north. \q Someone from the hills of Ephraim is announcing that disaster is coming.

es.L: Porque una voz anuncia desde Dan, \q y proclama calamidad desde la región montañosa de Efraín.
es.B: Porque una voz anuncia desde Dan, \q y proclama la desgracia desde la región montañosa de Efraín.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! Un mensajero trae noticias desde Dan, en el lejano norte. \q Alguien desde los montes de Efraín anuncia que la desgracia se acerca.

sw.L: Kwa maana sauti inatangaza kutoka Dani, \q na kuhubiri taabu kutoka nchi ya milima ya Efraimu.
sw.B: Kwa maana sauti inatangaza kutoka Dani, \q ikihubiri maafa kutoka nchi ya milima ya Efraimu.
sw.R: Sikilizeni! Mjumbe analeta habari kutoka Dani, upande wa kaskazini kabisa. \q Mtu kutoka milima ya Efraimu anatangaza kwamba maafa yanakuja.

decisions.choice: from Dan ... from the hill country of Ephraim: the news coming nearer and nearer
decisions.reason: Dan was the northernmost town of Israel ("from Dan to Beersheba", Judges 20:1). The hill country of Ephraim lies just north of Jerusalem and Benjamin. The report of the invader is passed south from town to town, each time closer.

decisions.choice: a voice: a messenger's shout, or simply "Listen!"
decisions.reason: The word means voice or sound and is often used as a call to attention, "Hark!" (3:21; 10:22). Here it is the shout of the one who brings the news.

decisions.choice: trouble: disaster
decisions.reason: The same word as "wickedness" in verse 14. Here it means the harm that is coming on them.

decisions.choice: Listen! A messenger ... in the far north
decisions.reason: Readable takes "a voice" as a call to attention and a messenger (m2), and says where Dan was (m1).

source.text: הַזְכִּ֣ירוּ לַגּוֹיִ֗ם הִנֵּה֙ הַשְׁמִ֣יעוּ עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם נֹצְרִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים מֵאֶ֣רֶץ הַמֶּרְחָ֑ק וַֽיִּתְּנ֛וּ עַל־עָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה קוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Make [it] known to the nations, look, proclaim against Jerusalem: Besiegers are coming from [the] land of the distance, and they have given against [the] cities of Judah their voice.

en.L: Make [it] known to the nations, look! Proclaim against Jerusalem: \q "Besiegers are coming from a distant land, \q and they raise their voice against the cities of Judah."
en.B: Report to the nations: look! Announce it against Jerusalem: \q "Besiegers are coming from a far country; \q they shout their war cry against the towns of Judah."
en.R: Warn the nations! Listen! Tell Jerusalem what is coming: \q "Enemies are coming from a land far away to surround the city. \q They are shouting their battle cries against the towns of Judah."

es.L: {{plural_you:Háganlo|Hacedlo}} saber a las naciones, ¡{{plural_you:miren|mirad}}! {{plural_you:Proclamen|Proclamad}} contra Jerusalén: \q «Sitiadores vienen de una tierra lejana, \q y alzan su voz contra las ciudades de Judá».
es.B: {{plural_you:Avisen|Avisad}} a las naciones: ¡{{plural_you:miren|mirad}}! {{plural_you:Anúncienlo|Anunciadlo}} contra Jerusalén: \q «Vienen sitiadores de un país lejano; \q lanzan su grito de guerra contra las ciudades de Judá».
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Adviertan|Advertid}} a las naciones! ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! {{plural_you:Díganle|Decidle}} a Jerusalén lo que se viene: \q «Vienen enemigos de una tierra lejana para rodear la ciudad. \q Lanzan sus gritos de guerra contra las ciudades de Judá».

sw.L: Yajulisheni mataifa, tazama! Hubirini juu ya Yerusalemu: \q "Wazingiraji wanakuja kutoka nchi ya mbali, \q nao wanapaza sauti yao juu ya miji ya Yuda."
sw.B: Yapeni mataifa habari: tazama! Tangazeni juu ya Yerusalemu: \q "Wazingiraji wanakuja kutoka nchi ya mbali; \q wanapiga kelele za vita juu ya miji ya Yuda."
sw.R: Yaonyeni mataifa! Sikilizeni! Iambieni Yerusalemu yanayokuja: \q "Maadui wanakuja kutoka nchi ya mbali kuuzunguka mji. \q Wanapiga kelele zao za vita dhidi ya miji ya Yuda."

decisions.choice: make it known: report, bring to notice
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause someone to remember or take note. The nations are to hear what is about to happen to Jerusalem, as witnesses to the LORD's judgment (6:18).

decisions.choice: besiegers: watchers, those who keep guard around a city
decisions.reason: The word means watchers or guards. Here it is the enemy who will surround the city and watch it so that no one gets in or out. Verse 17 plays on it: they are like watchmen around a field.

decisions.choice: they have given their voice: they raise the battle shout
decisions.reason: To "give voice" against a city is to shout the war cry before an attack (2:15, of lions roaring; 25:30).

decisions.choice: Enemies ... to surround the city
decisions.reason: Readable explains "besiegers" (m2).

source.text: כְּשֹׁמְרֵ֣י שָׂדַ֔י הָי֥וּ עָלֶ֖יהָ מִסָּבִ֑יב כִּי־אֹתִ֥י מָרָ֖תָה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Like keepers of a field they are against her all around, for me she has rebelled against, declares Yahweh.

en.L: Like guards of a field they are against her round about, \q for she has rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Like watchmen guarding a field they surround her, \q because she has rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: They surround Jerusalem like guards around a field, \q because she has turned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Como guardas de un campo están contra ella alrededor, \q porque contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} se rebeló, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Como centinelas que vigilan un campo la rodean, \q porque se ha rebelado contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Rodean a Jerusalén como guardias alrededor de un campo, \q porque ella se ha puesto en contra de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Kama walinzi wa shamba wako juu yake pande zote, \q kwa maana ameniasi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Kama walinzi wanaolinda shamba wanamzunguka, \q kwa sababu ameniasi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Wanauzunguka Yerusalemu kama walinzi wanaozunguka shamba, \q kwa sababu umeniasi, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: keepers of a field: watchmen posted around a field of crops
decisions.reason: Farmers set watchmen on every side of a field near harvest, to keep thieves and animals out (compare Isaiah 1:8). The besiegers will ring Jerusalem as closely, so that nothing passes.

decisions.choice: her ... she: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The pronouns are feminine and refer to Jerusalem, named in verse 16 and pictured as a woman, as again in verses 30-31.

decisions.choice: rebelled: defied, been bitterly disobedient
decisions.reason: The verb is used of defiance against God's word and command (5:23; Deuteronomy 1:26; 9:23).

decisions.choice: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names the city instead of "her" (m2).

source.text: דַּרְכֵּךְ֙ וּמַ֣עֲלָלַ֔יִךְ עָשׂ֥וֹ אֵ֖לֶּה לָ֑ךְ זֹ֤את רָעָתֵךְ֙ כִּ֣י מָ֔ר כִּ֥י נָגַ֖ע עַד־לִבֵּֽךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Your way and your deeds have done these to you; this [is] your evil, for [it is] bitter, for it has reached to your heart.

en.L: Your way and your deeds \q have done these things to you. \q This [is] your evil; how bitter [it is]! \q How it has reached to your heart!
en.B: Your conduct and your deeds \q have brought this on you. \q This is what your evil brings: how bitter it is, \q how it pierces to your heart!
en.R: The way you have lived and the things you have done \q have brought this on you. \q This disaster is what your evil has brought. It is bitter! \q It hurts you deep in your heart.

es.L: Tu camino y tus obras \q te han hecho estas cosas. \q Esta [es] tu maldad; ¡qué amarga [es]! \q ¡Cómo ha llegado hasta tu corazón!
es.B: Tu conducta y tus acciones \q te han traído esto. \q Esto es lo que trae tu maldad: ¡qué amargo es, \q cómo te atraviesa el corazón!
es.R: Tu manera de vivir y las cosas que has hecho \q te han traído esto. \q Esta desgracia es lo que tu maldad te ha traído. ¡Es amarga! \q Te duele en lo más hondo del corazón.

sw.L: Njia yako na matendo yako \q yamekutendea mambo haya. \q Huu [ndio] uovu wako; jinsi ulivyo mchungu! \q Jinsi ulivyofika mpaka moyoni mwako!
sw.B: Mwenendo wako na matendo yako \q yamekuletea haya. \q Hivi ndivyo uovu wako unavyoleta: jinsi ulivyo mchungu, \q jinsi unavyochoma mpaka moyoni mwako!
sw.R: Jinsi ulivyoishi na mambo uliyoyatenda \q yamekuletea haya. \q Maafa haya ndiyo uovu wako umeyaleta. Ni machungu! \q Yanakuumiza ndani kabisa ya moyo wako.

decisions.choice: your evil: your wickedness and the disaster it brings, both at once
decisions.reason: The word means both wrongdoing and calamity (verse 6). Here the two meet: the disaster is their own wickedness coming back on them, as 2:19 says, "your evil will discipline you".

decisions.choice: for ... for: "how" in an exclamation
decisions.reason: The small word usually means "for" or "that", but here it introduces two exclamations: how bitter it is, how it reaches the heart.

decisions.choice: it has reached to your heart: it strikes to the very center of you
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in verse 10 of the sword reaching the throat. Here the bitterness pierces to the heart, the center of life and thought.

decisions.choice: what your evil brings / This disaster is what your evil has brought
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the bare "your evil". Balanced and Readable spell out both sides of the word (m1): the disaster that their wrongdoing brought.

source.text: מֵעַ֣י׀מֵעַ֨י׀אוֹחִ֜ילָה קִיר֥וֹת לִבִּ֛י הֹֽמֶה־לִּ֥י לִבִּ֖י לֹ֣א אַחֲרִ֑ישׁ כִּ֣י ק֤וֹל שׁוֹפָר֙ שָׁמַ֣עַתְּ נַפְשִׁ֔י תְּרוּעַ֖ת מִלְחָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: My inward parts, my inward parts! I writhe! [The] walls of my heart! Is pounding to me my heart; not I can keep silent, for [the] sound of [the] shofar you have heard, my soul, [the] shout of war.

en.L: My bowels, my bowels! I writhe in pain! The walls of my heart! My heart is pounding within me; I cannot keep silent, \q for you have heard, my soul, the sound of the trumpet, \q the battle cry of war.
en.B: My insides, my insides! I twist in pain! My chest is bursting! My heart pounds within me; I cannot keep quiet, \q for you have heard it, my soul: the sound of the ram's horn, \q the battle cry of war.
en.R: Oh, the pain deep inside me! I am twisting in pain! My heart is pounding hard inside me. I cannot keep quiet, \q because I have heard the trumpet blowing. \q It is the alarm call for war.

es.L: ¡Mis entrañas, mis entrañas! ¡Me retuerzo de dolor! ¡Las paredes de mi corazón! Mi corazón palpita dentro de mí; no puedo callar, \q porque has oído, alma mía, el sonido de la trompeta, \q el grito de guerra.
es.B: ¡Mis entrañas, mis entrañas! ¡Me retuerzo de dolor! ¡El pecho me va a estallar! Mi corazón late con fuerza dentro de mí; no puedo callarme, \q porque lo has oído, alma mía: el sonido del cuerno de carnero, \q el grito de guerra.
es.R: ¡Ay, qué dolor tan hondo siento! ¡Me retuerzo de dolor! Mi corazón late con fuerza dentro de mí. No puedo quedarme callado, \q porque he oído el toque de la trompeta. \q Es la alarma de guerra.

sw.L: Matumbo yangu, matumbo yangu! Ninagaagaa kwa uchungu! Kuta za moyo wangu! Moyo wangu unadunda ndani yangu; siwezi kunyamaza, \q kwa maana umesikia, nafsi yangu, sauti ya baragumu, \q kelele ya vita.
sw.B: Ndani yangu, ndani yangu! Ninajipinda kwa maumivu! Kifua changu kinapasuka! Moyo wangu unadunda ndani yangu; siwezi kunyamaza, \q kwa maana umeisikia, ee nafsi yangu, sauti ya baragumu, \q kelele ya vita.
sw.R: Lo, maumivu yaliyo ndani yangu! Ninajipinda kwa maumivu! Moyo wangu unadunda sana ndani yangu. Siwezi kunyamaza, \q kwa sababu nimesikia baragumu likipigwa. \q Ni mwito wa vita.

decisions.choice: my inward parts: the depths of my feelings
decisions.reason: The word means the bowels or inner organs, the place where deep emotion is felt (Isaiah 16:11; Lamentations 1:20; Song of Songs 5:4). The cry is one of deep, physical anguish.

decisions.choice: the speaker: the prophet, crying out in anguish at what he sees coming
decisions.reason: Verses 19-21 are spoken by one person. It is most likely Jeremiah himself, overwhelmed by the vision of the invasion (8:18-23; 9:9). Because he speaks of "my tents" in verse 20, he also gives voice to the land and its people, whose ruin he shares. The LORD's answer comes in verse 22.

decisions.choice: I writhe ... you have heard, my soul: the forms read aloud in the tradition
alternatives: I wait ... I have heard, my soul
decisions.reason: In two places the Hebrew text has one form written and another marked to be read. In the first, both forms are usually taken as "I writhe"; the written one can also be read from a verb meaning "wait" or "hope". In the second, the written form is "I have heard", the form to be read is "you have heard, my soul". The sense is the same either way: the prophet himself has heard the alarm.

decisions.choice: the walls of my heart ... my heart is pounding: the heart hammering inside the chest
decisions.reason: The "walls" of the heart are the chest around it, or the heart itself pictured as a house. The verb is used of the roar of the sea and of a crowd: the heart is in turmoil.

decisions.choice: the sound of the shofar, the shout of war: the signals of battle
decisions.reason: The shofar sounded the alarm (verse 5), and the war cry was the shout raised as battle began (49:2; Amos 1:14).

decisions.choice: My insides ... My chest is bursting (B); the pain deep inside me (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "bowels" and "the walls of my heart", the Hebrew pictures. Balanced says "insides" and "my chest", the wall around the heart (m4), and Readable says what the cry means (m1).

decisions.choice: I have heard
decisions.reason: The prophet addresses his own soul, "you have heard, my soul", meaning "I myself have heard" (m3). Readable says "I have heard".

source.text: שֶׁ֤בֶר עַל־שֶׁ֨בֶר֙ נִקְרָ֔א כִּ֥י שֻׁדְּדָ֖ה כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ פִּתְאֹם֙ שֻׁדְּד֣וּ אֹהָלַ֔י רֶ֖גַע יְרִיעֹתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Destruction upon destruction is proclaimed, for is devastated all the land; suddenly are devastated my tents, [in] a moment my curtains.

en.L: Destruction upon destruction is proclaimed, \q for the whole land is devastated; \q suddenly my tents are devastated, \q in a moment my curtains.
en.B: Word comes of ruin upon ruin; \q the whole land lies devastated. \q Without warning my tents are torn down, \q my curtains in an instant.
en.R: News comes of one disaster after another. \q The whole country is destroyed. \q Suddenly my tents are destroyed. \q In a moment the curtains of my home are torn down.

es.L: Destrucción sobre destrucción se anuncia, \q porque toda la tierra está devastada; \q de repente son devastadas mis tiendas, \q en un momento mis cortinas.
es.B: Llegan noticias de ruina tras ruina; \q toda la tierra está devastada. \q Sin aviso han sido derribadas mis tiendas, \q en un instante mis cortinas.
es.R: Llegan noticias de una desgracia tras otra. \q Todo el país está destruido. \q De repente mis tiendas quedan destruidas. \q En un momento se rasgan las cortinas de mi casa.

sw.L: Uharibifu juu ya uharibifu unatangazwa, \q kwa maana nchi yote imeharibiwa; \q ghafla hema zangu zimeharibiwa, \q mapazia yangu kwa dakika moja.
sw.B: Habari zinakuja za maangamizi juu ya maangamizi; \q nchi yote imeharibiwa. \q Ghafla hema zangu zimebomolewa, \q mapazia yangu kwa kufumba na kufumbua.
sw.R: Habari zinakuja za maafa moja baada ya jingine. \q Nchi yote imeharibiwa. \q Ghafla hema zangu zimeharibiwa. \q Mara moja mapazia ya nyumba yangu yamechanwa.

decisions.choice: destruction upon destruction is proclaimed: one report of disaster follows another
decisions.reason: The word is the "great destruction" of verse 6, a breaking or crash. "Is proclaimed" means it is announced, or cried out: news of each new collapse comes in after the last.

decisions.choice: my tents ... my curtains: my home
decisions.reason: Tents and their curtains were an old way of speaking of one's home, even for people living in houses (10:20; 2 Samuel 20:1). The speaker's own household is struck as the land falls (m2 at verse 19).

decisions.choice: News comes of
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take "is proclaimed" as the arrival of reports (m1).

decisions.choice: the curtains of my home
decisions.reason: Readable adds "of my home" to show what the tents stand for (m2).

source.text: עַד־מָתַ֖י אֶרְאֶה־נֵּ֑ס אֶשְׁמְעָ֖ה ק֥וֹל שׁוֹפָֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Until when will I see a signal flag, will I hear [the] sound of [the] shofar?

en.L: How long must I see the signal flag, \q [and] hear the sound of the trumpet?
en.B: How long must I look at the signal flag \q and listen to the ram's horn?
en.R: How long must I see the signal flags of war \q and hear the trumpet calling to battle?

es.L: ¿Hasta cuándo veré la bandera, \q [y] oiré el sonido de la trompeta?
es.B: ¿Hasta cuándo tendré que mirar la bandera \q y escuchar el cuerno de carnero?
es.R: ¿Hasta cuándo tendré que ver las banderas de guerra \q y oír la trompeta que llama a la batalla?

sw.L: Hata lini nitaiona bendera, \q [na] kuisikia sauti ya baragumu?
sw.B: Nitaitazama bendera hadi lini, \q na kulisikiliza baragumu?
sw.R: Nitaziona bendera za vita hadi lini, \q na kusikia baragumu likiita watu vitani?

decisions.choice: the signal flag and the shofar: the signs of war going on
decisions.reason: The same flag and horn that called the people to flee (verses 5-6) now mark a war that seems never to end. The question "how long" is a lament (12:4; Psalm 13:2).

decisions.choice: of war ... calling to battle
decisions.reason: Readable says what the flag and the trumpet signal (m1).

source.text: כִּ֣י׀אֱוִ֣יל עַמִּ֗י אוֹתִי֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ בָּנִ֤ים סְכָלִים֙ הֵ֔מָּה וְלֹ֥א נְבוֹנִ֖ים הֵ֑מָּה חֲכָמִ֥ים הֵ֨מָּה֙ לְהָרַ֔ע וּלְהֵיטִ֖יב לֹ֥א יָדָֽעוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For foolish [is] my people; me they do not know; children stupid [are] they, and not understanding [are] they; wise [are] they to do evil, but to do good they do not know.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people are foolish; {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} they do not know; \q they are stupid children, \q and they have no understanding. \q They are wise at doing evil, \q but to do good they do not know [how].
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people are fools; they do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q They are senseless children; \q they have no understanding. \q They are skilled at doing evil, \q but they do not know how to do good.
en.R: This is happening because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people are foolish. They do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q They are like silly children \q who understand nothing. \q They are experts at doing wrong, \q but they do not know how to do what is right.

es.L: Porque necio [es] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo; a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conocen; \q son hijos insensatos, \q y no tienen entendimiento. \q Son sabios para hacer el mal, \q pero hacer el bien no saben.
es.B: Porque {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo es necio; no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conocen. \q Son hijos sin juicio; \q no tienen entendimiento. \q Son hábiles para hacer el mal, \q pero no saben hacer el bien.
es.R: Esto sucede porque {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo es necio. No {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conocen. \q Son como niños tontos \q que no entienden nada. \q Son expertos en hacer lo malo, \q pero no saben hacer lo que es bueno.

sw.L: Kwa maana watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ni wapumbavu; {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hawanijui; \q ni watoto wajinga, \q wala hawana ufahamu. \q Wana hekima ya kutenda mabaya, \q lakini kutenda mema hawajui.
sw.B: Kwa maana watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ni wapumbavu; hawanijui. \q Ni watoto wasio na akili; \q hawana ufahamu. \q Ni stadi wa kutenda mabaya, \q lakini hawajui kutenda mema.
sw.R: Haya yanatokea kwa sababu watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ni wapumbavu. Hawanijui. \q Ni kama watoto wajinga \q wasioelewa chochote. \q Ni wataalamu wa kutenda mabaya, \q lakini hawajui jinsi ya kutenda yaliyo mema.

decisions.choice: my people ... me: the LORD answers the prophet's lament
decisions.reason: The speaker changes from the prophet (verses 19-21) to the LORD, who gives the reason for the disaster. The word "for" ties his answer to the cry "how long".

decisions.choice: know: acknowledge, be in a close relationship with
decisions.reason: To know the LORD is more than knowing facts about him: it is to trust and obey him and live in his covenant (2:8; 9:23; 22:16; Hosea 4:1).

decisions.choice: foolish, stupid, without understanding: moral folly, not lack of intelligence
decisions.reason: The words describe people who have the wit to plan evil well but refuse to live wisely before God (Proverbs 1:7). They are clever in the wrong things.

decisions.choice: This is happening because
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "for" points back to: the disaster of verses 19-21 (m1).

source.text: רָאִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהִנֵּה־תֹ֖הוּ וָבֹ֑הוּ וְאֶל־הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֵ֥ין אוֹרָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: I looked at the earth, and look, formlessness and emptiness; and to the heavens, and there was not their light.

en.L: I looked at the earth, and look, [it was] formlessness and emptiness; \q and to the heavens, and their light [was] not [there].
en.B: I looked at the earth, and it was without form and empty; \q I looked to the heavens, and their light was gone.
en.R: I looked at the earth. It did not have any shape, and it was empty. \q I looked up at the sky, and there was no light.

es.L: Miré la tierra, y he aquí [que era] caos y vacío; \q y a los cielos, y no [había] su luz.
es.B: Miré la tierra, y estaba sin forma y vacía; \q miré los cielos, y su luz había desaparecido.
es.R: Miré la tierra. No tenía forma, y estaba vacía. \q Miré hacia el cielo, y no había luz.

sw.L: Niliitazama nchi, na tazama, [ilikuwa] ukiwa na utupu; \q na mbingu, na nuru yao haikuwako.
sw.B: Niliitazama dunia, nayo ilikuwa bila umbo, tena tupu; \q nilitazama mbingu, na nuru yake ilikuwa imetoweka.
sw.R: Niliitazama dunia. Haikuwa na umbo lolote, nayo ilikuwa tupu. \q Nilitazama juu angani, na hapakuwa na nuru.

decisions.choice: formless and empty, with no light: the world as it was before God's first word in Genesis 1:2-3
decisions.reason: The rhyming pair of words appears together only here and in Genesis 1:2 (Isaiah 34:11 sets them in parallel lines). In Genesis the earth was formless and empty and dark until God said, "Let there be light". In Jeremiah's vision the judgment runs creation backward: the land returns to that state, and the light is gone.

decisions.choice: I looked ... and look: a vision, told in four matching lines
decisions.reason: Verses 23-26 each begin "I looked, and look". The prophet describes what he saw in a vision of the coming judgment; the repeated words give it the shape of a poem in four stanzas.

decisions.choice: the earth: the whole earth in the vision
decisions.reason: The word can mean the land or the whole earth. Set beside "the heavens" and the words of Genesis 1:2, it is the earth in this vision, although the judgment it pictures falls on Judah (verses 26-27).

decisions.choice: formlessness and emptiness (L); without form and empty (B); did not have any shape ... empty (R)
decisions.reason: Each level uses its own wording from Genesis 1:2, so that a reader of either passage hears the other (m1).

decisions.choice: (look left out) ... I looked to the heavens / I looked up at the sky
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out the second "look", which Literal keeps, and repeat "I looked" where the Hebrew lets it be understood.

decisions.choice: "caos y vacío" (L); "sin forma y vacía" (B); "No tenía forma, y estaba vacía" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of Genesis 1:2 (tohu wabohu); each level keeps the wording a reader can hear as an echo of creation undone, following the English levels. Balanced and Readable leave out "he aquí", as the English does.

decisions.choice: ukiwa na utupu (Literal); bila umbo, tena tupu (Balanced); haikuwa na umbo ... tupu (Readable)
decisions.reason: The words of the world before creation (Genesis 1:2, meaning decision m1) worded so the echo can be heard at each level.

source.text: רָאִ֨יתִי֙ הֶֽהָרִ֔ים וְהִנֵּ֖ה רֹעֲשִׁ֑ים וְכָל־הַגְּבָע֖וֹת הִתְקַלְקָֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: I looked at the mountains, and look, quaking; and all the hills shook to and fro.

en.L: I looked at the mountains, and look, [they were] quaking, \q and all the hills were swaying.
en.B: I looked at the mountains, and they were quaking; \q all the hills were rocking back and forth.
en.R: I looked at the mountains, and they were shaking. \q All the hills were swaying back and forth.

es.L: Miré los montes, y he aquí [que] temblaban, \q y todas las colinas se tambaleaban.
es.B: Miré los montes, y estaban temblando; \q todas las colinas se mecían de un lado a otro.
es.R: Miré los montes, y estaban temblando. \q Todas las colinas se movían de un lado a otro.

sw.L: Niliitazama milima, na tazama, [ilikuwa] ikitetemeka, \q na vilima vyote vilikuwa vikiyumbayumba.
sw.B: Niliitazama milima, nayo ilikuwa ikitetemeka; \q vilima vyote vilikuwa vikiyumba huku na huko.
sw.R: Niliitazama milima, nayo ilikuwa ikitikisika. \q Vilima vyote vilikuwa vikiyumba huku na huko.

decisions.choice: the mountains quaking: even what is most firm gives way
decisions.reason: Mountains stand for what is solid and lasting (Psalm 46:3-4; Isaiah 54:10). When the LORD comes in judgment they shake (Nahum 1:5; Judges 5:5).

decisions.choice: shook to and fro: swayed lightly back and forth
decisions.reason: The verb comes from a root meaning "light". The hills rock as if they had no weight.

decisions.choice: (look left out)
decisions.reason: As in verse 23, Balanced and Readable leave out "look", which Literal keeps.

source.text: רָאִ֕יתִי וְהִנֵּ֖ה אֵ֣ין הָאָדָ֑ם וְכָל־ע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם נָדָֽדוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: I looked, and look, there was not the human, and all [the] birds of the heavens had fled.

en.L: I looked, and look, there was no human being, \q and all the birds of the heavens had fled.
en.B: I looked, and there was no one at all; \q every bird in the sky had flown away.
en.R: I looked, and there were no people. \q All the birds had flown away.

es.L: Miré, y he aquí [que] no había ser humano, \q y todas las aves de los cielos habían huido.
es.B: Miré, y no había nadie; \q todas las aves del cielo se habían ido volando.
es.R: Miré, y no había gente. \q Todas las aves se habían ido volando.

sw.L: Nilitazama, na tazama, hapakuwa na mwanadamu, \q na ndege wote wa angani walikuwa wamekimbia.
sw.B: Nilitazama, wala hapakuwa na mtu hata mmoja; \q kila ndege wa angani alikuwa ameruka akaenda zake.
sw.R: Nilitazama, wala hapakuwa na watu. \q Ndege wote walikuwa wameruka wakaenda zao.

decisions.choice: no human, no birds: the creatures of the fifth and sixth days gone
decisions.reason: In Genesis 1 the birds were made on the fifth day and humankind on the sixth (Genesis 1:20, 26-27). The vision takes them away again (compare 9:9; Zephaniah 1:3; Hosea 4:3).

decisions.choice: the human: humankind, people
decisions.reason: The word with the article means humankind as a whole, men and women alike, not one man.

decisions.choice: (look left out)
decisions.reason: As in verse 23.

source.text: רָאִ֕יתִי וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַכַּרְמֶ֖ל הַמִּדְבָּ֑ר וְכָל־עָרָ֗יו נִתְּצוּ֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י חֲר֥וֹן אַפּֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: I looked, and look, the orchard land [was] the wilderness, and all its cities were pulled down before Yahweh, before [the] burning of his anger.

en.L: I looked, and look, the orchard land [was] the wilderness, \q and all its cities were pulled down before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} burning anger.
en.B: I looked, and the orchard land had become a desert; \q all its towns had been torn down before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fierce anger.
en.R: I looked, and the land of rich orchards had become a desert. \q All its towns had been torn down. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had done this in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fierce anger.

es.L: Miré, y he aquí [que] la tierra de huertos [era] el desierto, \q y todas sus ciudades estaban derribadas delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, \q delante del ardor de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira.
es.B: Miré, y la tierra de huertos se había vuelto un desierto; \q todas sus ciudades habían sido derribadas ante {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q ante {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ardiente ira.
es.R: Miré, y la tierra de ricos huertos se había convertido en un desierto. \q Todas sus ciudades habían sido derribadas. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo había hecho en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ardiente ira.

sw.L: Nilitazama, na tazama, nchi ya bustani [ilikuwa] jangwa, \q na miji yake yote ilikuwa imebomolewa mbele ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q mbele ya hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kali.
sw.B: Nilitazama, na nchi ya bustani ilikuwa imekuwa jangwa; \q miji yake yote ilikuwa imebomolewa mbele ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q mbele ya hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kali.
sw.R: Nilitazama, na nchi ya bustani nyingi za matunda ilikuwa imekuwa jangwa. \q Miji yake yote ilikuwa imebomolewa. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amefanya hivyo katika hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kali.

decisions.choice: the orchard land: the fertile, cultivated land
decisions.reason: The word means garden land, land planted with vines and fruit trees. In 2:7 the LORD brought Israel "into a land of orchards". It is not Mount Carmel here, since it is set against the desert as fruitful land against barren.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: the fruitful land has become the desert itself
decisions.reason: The two nouns stand side by side with no verb: the garden land "was the wilderness". It is the reverse of the promise that the desert would become a garden (Isaiah 32:15; 35:1-2).

decisions.choice: before the LORD, before his burning anger: at his presence, by his anger
decisions.reason: "Before" (literally "from the face of") means "because of, at the coming of". The ruin is the LORD's work, the fierce anger named in verse 8.

decisions.choice: the orchard land (L, B); the land of rich orchards (R)
decisions.reason: The word is "orchard" at every level, as in Isaiah. Here it names the whole fertile land (m1), so all three levels say "land".

decisions.choice: The LORD had done this
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "before the LORD" means (m3).

source.text: כִּי־כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שְׁמָמָ֥ה תִהְיֶ֖ה כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְכָלָ֖ה לֹ֥א אֶעֱשֶֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: For thus says Yahweh: A desolation will be all the land, but a full end not I will make.

en.L: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q A desolation the whole land will be, \q yet a full end I will not make.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q The whole land will be laid waste, \q but I will not destroy it completely.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q The whole land will be ruined, \q but I will not destroy it completely.

es.L: Porque así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: \q Desolación será toda la tierra, \q pero no haré un exterminio total.
es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: \q Toda la tierra quedará desolada, \q pero no la destruiré por completo.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: \q Toda la tierra quedará arruinada, \q pero no la destruiré por completo.

sw.L: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: \q Ukiwa itakuwa nchi yote, \q lakini ukomo kamili sitafanya.
sw.B: Kwa maana hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: \q Nchi yote itaharibiwa, \q lakini sitaiangamiza kabisa.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: \q Nchi yote itaharibiwa, \q lakini sitaiangamiza kabisa.

decisions.choice: a full end: complete destruction, an end with nothing left
decisions.reason: The word means a finishing off, destruction to the last. The same promise, that the LORD will not make a full end, returns in 5:10, 18; 30:11 and 46:28: judgment will be severe, but a remnant will be left.

decisions.choice: but ... not: a limit set within the judgment
alternatives: and I will make a full end of it (a change of one letter)
