decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "not". It has been suggested that the word be read with a different letter as "of it", which would make the line a threat of total destruction. The text as it stands is kept, and the same promise in 5:10 and 5:18 supports it.

decisions.choice: the land: the land of Judah
decisions.reason: The same word as "the earth" in verses 23 and 28. Here, with the cities of verse 26, it is the land that will be laid waste.

decisions.choice: destroy it completely
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "make a full end" as a plain verb.

source.text: עַל־זֹאת֙ תֶּאֱבַ֣ל הָאָ֔רֶץ וְקָדְר֥וּ הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם מִמָּ֑עַל עַ֤ל כִּי־דִבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ זַמֹּ֔תִי וְלֹ֥א נִחַ֖מְתִּי וְלֹא־אָשׁ֥וּב מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: Because of this will mourn the earth, and will grow dark the heavens above, because I have spoken, I have purposed, and not I have relented, and not I will turn back from it.

en.L: On account of this the earth will mourn, \q and the heavens above will grow dark, \q because I have spoken, I have resolved, \q and I have not relented, and I will not turn back from it.
en.B: For this the earth will mourn, \q and the sky above will turn dark, \q because I have spoken and I have decided; \q I have not changed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mind, and I will not turn back from it.
en.R: Because of this, the earth will mourn, \q and the sky will grow dark. \q I have spoken, and I have made up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mind. \q I will not change it, and I will not turn back.

es.L: Por esto se enlutará la tierra, \q y se oscurecerán los cielos arriba, \q porque he hablado, lo he decidido, \q y no me he retractado, ni me volveré atrás.
es.B: Por esto la tierra estará de luto, \q y el cielo allá arriba se oscurecerá, \q porque he hablado y lo he decidido; \q no he cambiado de parecer, y no me volveré atrás.
es.R: Por eso la tierra estará de luto, \q y el cielo se oscurecerá. \q He hablado, y he tomado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} decisión. \q No la cambiaré, y no me volveré atrás.

sw.L: Kwa sababu ya hili nchi itaomboleza, \q na mbingu juu zitakuwa giza, \q kwa sababu nimesema, nimekusudia, \q wala sijaghairi, wala sitarudi nyuma.
sw.B: Kwa sababu hii dunia itaomboleza, \q na anga la juu litatiwa giza, \q kwa sababu nimesema na nimeamua; \q sijaghairi, wala sitarudi nyuma.
sw.R: Kwa sababu hii, dunia itaomboleza, \q na anga litakuwa giza. \q Nimesema, na nimeamua. \q Sitabadili nia {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, wala sitarudi nyuma.

decisions.choice: the earth will mourn, the heavens grow dark: all creation grieves at the judgment
decisions.reason: The earth is pictured as a mourner and the sky as putting on dark clothes of grief (12:4; Isaiah 50:3; Hosea 4:3; Joel 2:10). The word "earth" here, as in verse 23, is wider than the land of verse 27.

decisions.choice: purposed: planned, resolved
decisions.reason: The verb means to form a plan and hold to it (51:12; Lamentations 2:17).

decisions.choice: I have not relented: I have not changed my course
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the LORD turning from a judgment he had announced when people repent (18:8; 26:3, 13, 19; Jonah 3:10). Here, with Judah unrepentant, he will not turn back.

decisions.choice: changed my mind / I will not change it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "relent" in everyday words.

decisions.choice: "no me he retractado" (L); "no he cambiado de parecer" (B); "No la cambiaré" (R)
decisions.reason: God's relenting is never "arrepentirse", as the Samuel terms note sets; Literal says "retractarse"; Balanced and Readable say he has not changed his mind, as the English levels do. The English Balanced has a deity_pronoun span on "my mind"; Spanish "cambiar de parecer" has no free pronoun, so Balanced has none.

source.text: מִקּ֨וֹל פָּרָ֜שׁ וְרֹ֣מֵה קֶ֗שֶׁת בֹּרַ֨חַת֙ כָּל־הָעִ֔יר בָּ֚אוּ בֶּעָבִ֔ים וּבַכֵּפִ֖ים עָל֑וּ כָּל־הָעִ֣יר עֲזוּבָ֔ה וְאֵין־יוֹשֵׁ֥ב בָּהֵ֖ן אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: From [the] sound of horseman and shooter of bow fleeing [is] every the city; they go into thickets and among rocks they climb up; every the city [is] forsaken, and there is not dwelling in them a man.

en.L: At the sound of horseman and bowman \q every city is fleeing; \q they go into the thickets, and among the rocks they climb; \q every city is forsaken, \q and no one lives in them.
en.B: At the sound of horsemen and archers \q the people of every town run away. \q They go into the thickets; they climb up among the rocks. \q Every town is abandoned; \q no one lives in them.
en.R: When they hear the horsemen and the archers coming, \q the people in every town run away. \q They hide in the bushes and climb up among the rocks. \q All the towns are left empty. \q No one lives in them anymore.

es.L: Al ruido del jinete y del arquero \q huye toda la ciudad; \q se meten en los matorrales, y entre las peñas suben; \q toda ciudad está abandonada, \q y no habita en ellas nadie.
es.B: Al ruido de los jinetes y los arqueros \q la gente de cada ciudad huye. \q Se meten en los matorrales; trepan entre las peñas. \q Todas las ciudades están abandonadas; \q nadie vive en ellas.
es.R: Cuando oyen venir a los jinetes y a los arqueros, \q la gente de cada ciudad sale huyendo. \q Se esconden en los matorrales y trepan entre las rocas. \q Todas las ciudades quedan vacías. \q Ya nadie vive en ellas.

sw.L: Kwa sauti ya mpanda farasi na mpiga upinde \q kila mji unakimbia; \q wanaingia vichakani, na kati ya miamba wanapanda; \q kila mji umeachwa, \q wala hakuna mtu anayekaa ndani yake.
sw.B: Kwa sauti ya wapanda farasi na wapiga mishale \q watu wa kila mji wanakimbia. \q Wanaingia vichakani; wanapanda kati ya miamba. \q Kila mji umeachwa; \q hakuna anayeishi ndani yake.
sw.R: Wanapowasikia wapanda farasi na wapiga mishale wakija, \q watu wa kila mji wanakimbia. \q Wanajificha vichakani na kupanda kati ya miamba. \q Miji yote imeachwa tupu. \q Hakuna mtu anayeishi humo tena.

decisions.choice: every the city: every city, the people of each town
decisions.reason: The words can mean "the whole city", but "in them" at the end of the verse shows that many towns are meant. The town stands for its people, who flee.

decisions.choice: thickets ... rocks: dense brush and rocky crags, places to hide
decisions.reason: The first word is rare and seems to mean thick undergrowth; the second means rocks or cliffs. In times of invasion people hid in caves, thickets and rocks (1 Samuel 13:6; Isaiah 2:19, 21).

decisions.choice: horseman and archer: the enemy's cavalry and bowmen
decisions.reason: The armies of Mesopotamia fought with horsemen, chariots and archers (6:23; 50:42). The words are singular, standing for the whole force.

decisions.choice: the people of every town
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the people" of each town flee (m1).

source.text: וְאַ֨תְּ שָׁד֜וּד מַֽה־תַּעֲשִׂ֗י כִּֽי־תִלְבְּשִׁ֨י שָׁנִ֜י כִּי־תַעְדִּ֣י עֲדִי־זָהָ֗ב כִּֽי־תִקְרְעִ֤י בַפּוּךְ֙ עֵינַ֔יִךְ לַשָּׁ֖וְא תִּתְיַפִּ֑י מָאֲסוּ־בָ֥ךְ עֹגְבִ֖ים נַפְשֵׁ֥ךְ יְבַקֵּֽשׁוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, devastated [one], what will you do? That you dress [in] scarlet, that you adorn [yourself with] ornaments of gold, that you enlarge with eye paint your eyes, in vain you make yourself beautiful; reject you lovers; your life they seek.

en.L: And you, devastated one, what will you do? Though you dress in scarlet, though you adorn [yourself with] ornaments of gold, though you enlarge your eyes with paint, \q in vain you make yourself beautiful. \q [Your] lovers reject you; they seek your life.
en.B: And you, ruined one, what will you do? Though you dress in scarlet, though you put on jewelry of gold, though you make your eyes look large with paint, \q you make yourself beautiful for nothing. \q Your lovers reject you; they are out to take your life.
en.R: And you, Jerusalem, now ruined, what will you do? You may dress in bright red clothes and wear gold jewelry. You may paint around your eyes to make them look bigger. \q But it is no use making yourself beautiful. \q The nations you tried to win as lovers hate you now. They want to kill you.

es.L: Y tú, devastada, ¿qué harás? Aunque te vistas de escarlata, aunque te adornes [con] joyas de oro, aunque agrandes tus ojos con pintura, \q en vano te embelleces. \q [Tus] amantes te desprecian; buscan tu vida.
es.B: Y tú, arruinada, ¿qué harás? Aunque te vistas de escarlata, aunque te pongas joyas de oro, aunque te pintes los ojos para que se vean grandes, \q te embelleces para nada. \q Tus amantes te desprecian; quieren quitarte la vida.
es.R: Y tú, Jerusalén, ahora arruinada, ¿qué harás? Puedes vestirte de rojo brillante y ponerte joyas de oro. Puedes pintarte alrededor de los ojos para que se vean más grandes. \q Pero no sirve de nada que te pongas hermosa. \q Las naciones que quisiste ganarte como amantes ahora te odian. Quieren matarte.

sw.L: Nawe, uliyeangamizwa, utafanya nini? Ingawa unavaa nguo nyekundu, ingawa unajipamba [kwa] mapambo ya dhahabu, ingawa unayapanua macho yako kwa wanja, \q bure unajifanya mzuri. \q Wapenzi [wako] wanakukataa; wanautafuta uhai wako.
sw.B: Nawe uliyeharibiwa, utafanya nini? Ingawa unavaa nguo nyekundu, ingawa unajivika vito vya dhahabu, ingawa unapaka wanja macho yako yaonekane makubwa, \q unajirembesha bure. \q Wapenzi wako wanakukataa; wanataka kukuua.
sw.R: Nawe Yerusalemu, uliyeharibiwa sasa, utafanya nini? Unaweza kuvaa nguo nyekundu na kuvaa vito vya dhahabu. Unaweza kupaka wanja macho yako yaonekane makubwa. \q Lakini haifai kitu kujifanya mzuri. \q Mataifa uliyojaribu kuyapata kama wapenzi sasa yanakuchukia. Yanataka kukuua.

decisions.choice: you, devastated one: Jerusalem, spoken to as a woman
decisions.reason: The words are feminine singular, addressed to the city, which is named "the daughter of Zion" in verse 31. She is spoken of as already ruined, so sure is the judgment.

decisions.choice: scarlet, gold ornaments, eye paint: a woman dressing to attract
decisions.reason: Rich red cloth, gold jewelry and dark paint around the eyes were signs of wealth and beauty. Jezebel painted her eyes before she met Jehu (2 Kings 9:30), and Ezekiel 23:40 uses the same picture for Jerusalem courting other nations.

decisions.choice: lovers: the foreign nations Judah courted as allies
decisions.reason: Jeremiah pictures Judah's search for help from Egypt and Assyria as a woman chasing lovers (2:33, 36; 3:1; 22:20; 30:14). Those she courted will turn on her.

decisions.choice: they seek your life: they want to kill you
decisions.reason: To "seek someone's life" means to try to kill them (11:21; 19:7; Exodus 4:19).

decisions.choice: that ... that ... that: even though you do these things
decisions.reason: The three clauses with the small word usually meaning "that" or "for" set out what she does, and the line "in vain you make yourself beautiful" answers them all: none of it will help.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem ... The nations you tried to win as lovers
decisions.reason: Readable names the city (m1) and explains who the lovers are (m3).

source.text: כִּי֩ ק֨וֹל כְּחוֹלָ֜ה שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי צָרָה֙ כְּמַבְכִּירָ֔ה ק֧וֹל בַּת־צִיּ֛וֹן תִּתְיַפֵּ֖חַ תְּפָרֵ֣שׂ כַּפֶּ֑יהָ אֽוֹי־נָ֣א לִ֔י כִּֽי־עָיְפָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֖י לְהֹרְגִֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: For a voice like [one] in labor I have heard, distress like [one] bearing a first child, [the] voice of [the] daughter of Zion; she gasps for breath, she spreads out her palms: Woe now to me, for faints my soul before killers!

en.L: For a cry as of [a woman] in labor I have heard, distress as of [one] bearing her first child, \q the cry of the daughter of Zion; she gasps for breath, she spreads out her hands: \q "Woe [is] me now, \q for my soul faints before killers!"
en.B: I hear a scream like that of a woman in labor, the agony of one bearing her first child: \q it is the voice of Daughter Zion, fighting for breath and holding out her hands: \q "Woe is me! \q My life is ebbing away before killers!"
en.R: I hear a cry like a woman giving birth, the painful cry of a woman having her first baby. \q It is the cry of the people of Zion, like a woman gasping for breath and reaching out her hands for help: \q "How terrible this is for me! \q I am fainting, and murderers are all around me!"

es.L: Porque un grito como de [mujer] de parto he oído, angustia como de [la que] da a luz a su primer hijo, \q el grito de la hija de Sion; jadea, extiende sus manos: \q «¡Ay de mí ahora, \q porque mi alma desfallece ante los asesinos!».
es.B: Oigo un grito como el de una mujer de parto, la angustia de la que da a luz a su primer hijo: \q es la voz de la hija de Sion, que lucha por respirar y extiende las manos: \q «¡Ay de mí! \q ¡Mi vida se apaga ante los asesinos!».
es.R: Oigo un grito como el de una mujer que da a luz, el grito de dolor de una mujer que tiene su primer bebé. \q Es el grito del pueblo de Sion, como una mujer que jadea y extiende las manos pidiendo ayuda: \q «¡Qué terrible es esto para mí! \q ¡Me desmayo, y los asesinos me rodean!».

sw.L: Kwa maana nimesikia sauti kama ya [mwanamke] aliye na utungu, dhiki kama ya [yule] anayezaa mtoto wake wa kwanza, \q sauti ya binti Sayuni; anatweta, anainyosha mikono yake: \q "Ole wangu sasa, \q kwa maana nafsi yangu inazimia mbele ya wauaji!"
sw.B: Ninasikia kilio kama cha mwanamke mwenye utungu, maumivu ya yule anayezaa mtoto wake wa kwanza: \q ni sauti ya Binti Sayuni, akitweta na kuinyosha mikono yake: \q "Ole wangu! \q Uhai wangu unanitoka mbele ya wauaji!"
sw.R: Ninasikia kilio kama cha mwanamke anayezaa, kilio cha uchungu cha mwanamke anayezaa mtoto wake wa kwanza. \q Ni kilio cha watu wa Sayuni, kama mwanamke anayetweta na kunyosha mikono yake kuomba msaada: \q "Mambo ni mabaya sana kwangu! \q Ninazimia, na wauaji wamenizunguka pande zote!"

decisions.choice: like a woman in labor with her first child: helpless, overwhelming anguish
decisions.reason: The pain of childbirth is the prophets' picture for terror that cannot be escaped (6:24; 13:21; 22:23; 30:6; Isaiah 13:8). A first birth was known to be the hardest and most frightening.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Zion: Jerusalem and its people, pictured as a young woman
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah 1:8, Zion stands for Jerusalem, and "daughter" pictures the city and its people as a woman, loved and vulnerable. Here the picture is of a woman in labor who finds herself among killers.

decisions.choice: she spreads out her palms: a gesture of pleading for help
decisions.reason: Spreading out the hands was a gesture of prayer or of begging for help (Lamentations 1:17; Isaiah 1:15). Here no help comes.

decisions.choice: my soul faints before killers: my life is ebbing away in front of those who will kill me
decisions.reason: "Soul" means the self or life, and the verb means to be weary or faint. The murderers stand over her as she gives birth.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Zion (L); Daughter Zion (B); the people of Zion (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording, as in Isaiah. Readable says "the people of Zion" and keeps the picture of one woman with "like a woman", so that "her hands" and "me" still fit (m2).

decisions.choice: Woe is me (L, B); How terrible this is for me (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for a cry of woe said of oneself, as in Isaiah. Literal also keeps the small word "now", which strengthens the cry.

decisions.choice: for help ... are all around me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the outstretched hands mean (m3) and where the killers are (m4).

decisions.choice: "la hija de Sion" (L, B); "el pueblo de Sion" (R)
decisions.reason: Daughter Zion as the terms note sets it for Spanish.

decisions.choice: binti Sayuni (Literal); Binti Sayuni (Balanced); watu wa Sayuni (Readable)
decisions.reason: Daughter Zion worded as the terms note and 2 Kings 19:21.

decisions.choice: Ole wangu (Literal, Balanced); Mambo ni mabaya sana kwangu (Readable)
decisions.reason: The cry of woe over oneself, worded as the terms note sets it (1 Kings 13:30).
